d1_6: Your little one will still be there later. Some people want out of the whole inner-child idea, though ("this just isn't me"), and that's a different thing. If that's you, I wouldn't keep sneaking it back in through some "gentler" version, or start calling the dishes reparenting. Looking after yourself and keeping yourself safe can happen in whatever words feel like yours. Same with figuring out where you're headed, and getting support from people.
d2_6: If you do want it, and it's just too much at this depth, some people try one technique after another, thinking, "I just have to push through this." I'd go shallower instead. If going inward keeps making it worse, or you're not sure you could stop and come back, I'd put the inward stuff down and come back out to the room. Once you're steadier, there's a harm-reduction saying for this: start low and go slow. Low might be doing one protective thing out in your life, or calling someone who's good for you. Or a short hello to your little one with your eyes open.
i1_6: Maybe part of what your little one went through was being alone with it. Then reaching toward people can be part of this work too, and you can call that reparenting if you like the word. Some people figure, "I'll get myself sorted out first, and then I'll be fit company for anybody." I don't think a decent parent would ask that of a lonely kid. So sometimes the grown-up thing to do is just to text someone first.
i2_6: I'd look for more than one place to belong, too. One partner or one therapist can't be all of it, and if they're busy or gone, you'd be left with nobody. Keep the good people you've got, and then maybe add a spiritual community that fits you, or a class you keep showing up to. Not every one of them has to click. But if a group makes you feel more wanted than you've ever felt, and then someone there starts saying your old friends are holding you back, I'd let the Protector handle that one, and keep your other people, even if it means not going back.
